Surface: infra

## Overview

The #2837 post-hoc `checkFirstCallArtifacts` check and the two-call gate it feeds currently treat a missing `config.yml` as first-failure-wins: any `missing-config` result routes straight to the two-call gate's §5 teardown, releasing the record as `pr-opened` and stranding a tested, correct PR outside pipeline review (the #3111/#3129/#3138/#3126 shape). This unit adds a `repairable` classification to the artifact check — `missing-config` plus an intact live claim and (under `pr-first`) an intact recorded/pushed PR becomes `repairable: true` — and adds a repair-then-continue branch to the two-call gate and its `sequential-execution.md` mirror: log the repair, dispatch call 2 unchanged, and let `/flow`'s own case-3 adoption rebuild `config.yml` through its sanctioned writer. Every other failure, and `missing-config` with `repairable: false`, keeps the existing §5 teardown.

**Complexity:** Medium
**Estimated tasks:** 6

## Non-Goals

- Changing the #2429 status-line check or its ordering — it still runs first, and a malformed status line is still `BLOCKED` regardless of this unit's repair branch.
- Building the dispatcher-bound run / `checkDispatchConfigGate` early checkpoint — a separate sub-issue of this same decomposition (file-overlap note: that sub-issue edits `sibling-session-check.md`, this one edits `sequential-execution.md` — deliberately disjoint files).
- Changing the first call's model profile — a separate sub-issue of this same decomposition.
- Relaxing the malformed-status-line case — the design doc notes the early checkpoint and the profile change make it rarer in practice, but this unit does not loosen that check.

## Current State

- `plugin/bin/lib/dispatch/first-call-artifact-check.js` — `checkFirstCallArtifacts` currently returns immediately on a `missing-config` result (first-failure-wins), without checking whether the claim and PR are otherwise intact.
- `plugin/skills/dispatch/two-call-gate.md` §2 — a failed artifact check with any `reason` currently routes to §5's teardown; there is no repair branch today.
- `plugin/skills/dispatch/sequential-execution.md` "The loop" (~line 30) — mirrors two-call-gate.md's §2/§5 logic for the sequential (non-parallel) dispatch path, and also carries a stale "`/claude-tweaks:flow {target} wrap-up`" teardown reference (~line 32) that §5 itself already replaced with a direct `/claude-tweaks:wrap-up {target} cleanup-only` (#1766) — this unit fixes both in the same pass since they're in the same file section.
- `plugin/skills/flow/steps-and-gates.md:72-80` (read-only) — documents adoption case 3 (`hasConfig` false, `hasOtherContent` true); `plugin/bin/lib/flow/preflight.js` (read-only) — `computeAdoption` is what returns case 3 for a run in this shape.
- `tests/bin-lib/dispatch/first-call-artifact-check.test.js` — the existing suite for `checkFirstCallArtifacts`; its current cases must stay byte-for-byte green after this unit's additive field lands.
- Suites that read the files this unit touches and must stay green: `tests/flow-cleanup-only-conformance.test.js`, `tests/build-already-shipped-exit.test.js`, `tests/dispatch-mechanical-enforcement.test.js`, `tests/dispatch-sequential-execution-conformance.test.js`, `tests/pr-first-merge.test.js`, `tests/dispatch-settle-and-merge-lazy-read.test.js`.

## Deliverables

- [ ] In `plugin/bin/lib/dispatch/first-call-artifact-check.js`, on a `missing-config` result, continue the remaining checks instead of returning immediately: the claim checks (live, `runId` matches the claim record's own `runId` — not read from `config.yml`, which is absent), and — when `integration-model` resolves to `pr-first` — the PR checks (recorded PR, branch recorded and pushed). The check's final return on this path is always `{ ok: false, reason: 'missing-config', repairable }` — a secondary check's own more specific failure reason (e.g. `claim-absent`, `pr-branch-unpushed`) is used only to compute `repairable`, never surfaced as a different top-level `reason` once `missing-config` has already fired. `repairable` is exactly `true` when, in order: the claim is live and its `runId` matches, AND (when `integration-model !== 'pr-first'`, the PR checks are skipped entirely and this condition is satisfied by the claim check alone) (when `integration-model === 'pr-first'`, the PR is recorded and its branch is pushed). Any other resolved `integration-model` value (unknown or future) is treated like non-`pr-first`: the strict `=== 'pr-first'` equality check already skips its PR branch for anything else, with no special-casing needed. Read `integration-model` via `plugin/bin/lib/policy-schema.js`'s `resolvePolicyConfig`/`resolvePolicyKeys` — **not** the defaulting `resolveIntegrationModel`, which falls through to `detectIntegrationModel` and is documented to never fail/never return null; `resolvePolicyKeys` is the one that can surface `invalid: true` or an unreadable/unparseable policy file, which AC 4 below requires to be reachable. `resolvePolicyConfig` needs a `repoRoot` the check does not currently take as input — reuse the same injected `git`/`readFile` deps `resolvePolicyConfig`'s other callers (`bin/resolve-policy.js`, `bin/lib/blast-radius-cli.js`) already inject, rather than adding a bespoke resolution path.
- [ ] Add a `repairable` boolean field to the check's return value: `true` exactly when every check in the enumerated set above (claim-live, claim-runId-match, and — `pr-first` only — PR-recorded, PR-branch-pushed) passes; `false` otherwise, including when the `resolvePolicyConfig`/`resolvePolicyKeys` read for `integration-model` fails (throws, or returns `invalid: true`). Every other failure reason keeps today's first-failure-wins return shape unchanged — `repairable` is a purely additive field that appears only alongside `reason: 'missing-config'`. Add a test or explicit comment cross-referencing that these same fields (claim liveness/`runId`, PR recorded/pushed) are exactly what `plugin/bin/lib/flow/preflight.js`'s `computeAdoption` needs to land a repaired run in adoption case 3 — not a superset or subset of its inputs.
- [ ] In `plugin/skills/dispatch/two-call-gate.md` §2, add the repair branch: a failed check with `reason: 'missing-config'` and `repairable: true` does not route to §5. Instead the dispatching session logs `AUTO {time} — Artifact check: config.yml missing, claim/PR intact — repairing via call 2's /flow case-3 adoption. Reversibility: high.` and dispatches call 2 unchanged — "unchanged" means byte-identical to the normal call-2 invocation, carrying no repair-context flag or hint; `/flow` self-detects adoption case 3 purely from on-disk state (`hasConfig: false`, `hasOtherContent: true`) exactly as it already does for any other case-3 adoption, so no new signal needs to be threaded through the dispatch call. Every other failure, and `missing-config` with `repairable: false`, keeps §5's existing teardown.
- [ ] Mirror the same repair branch into `plugin/skills/dispatch/sequential-execution.md`'s "The loop" (~line 30).
- [ ] In the same `sequential-execution.md` edit, fix the stale "`/claude-tweaks:flow {target} wrap-up`" teardown reference (~line 32) to §5's direct `/claude-tweaks:wrap-up {target} cleanup-only` (#1766).
- [ ] Add a test (or extend an existing ordering test covering `two-call-gate.md`/`sequential-execution.md`) asserting the #2429 status-line check still runs before the artifact check in both files — not just a narrative confirmation: a fixture with a malformed status line and an otherwise `repairable: true`-shaped artifact result must still resolve `BLOCKED`, never the repair branch.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A new test: `missing-config` + claim live and matching `runId` + (under `pr-first`) PR recorded and pushed → `checkFirstCallArtifacts` returns `repairable: true`.
2. A new test: `missing-config` + claim absent (or not live, or `runId` mismatch) → returns `repairable: false`.
3. A new test: `missing-config` + PR unpushed (or unrecorded, under `pr-first`) → returns `repairable: false`.
4. A new test: the `resolvePolicyConfig`/`resolvePolicyKeys` read for `integration-model` fails (throws, or resolves `invalid: true`) → returns `repairable: false` — it never repairs on missing evidence.
5. A new test: `missing-config` + claim live and matching `runId`, under `integration-model: local-merge` (or any value other than `pr-first`) → returns `repairable: true` from the claim checks alone, with the PR checks skipped entirely — the same non-`pr-first` skip the check logic already specifies, now pinned for the `repairable` computation too.
6. Every existing case in `tests/bin-lib/dispatch/first-call-artifact-check.test.js` stays byte-for-byte green — in particular, every failure reason other than `missing-config` has no `repairable` field at all, exactly as before this change.
7. `plugin/skills/dispatch/two-call-gate.md` §2 contains the repair branch described above, including the literal `AUTO {time} — Artifact check: config.yml missing, claim/PR intact — repairing via call 2's /flow case-3 adoption. Reversibility: high.` log-line template, pinned by a prose-conformance test (extend `tests/dispatch-mechanical-enforcement.test.js` if it already parses `two-call-gate.md`'s §2, else add a case to a dispatch prose-conformance suite).
8. `plugin/skills/dispatch/sequential-execution.md` "The loop" mirrors the same repair branch, and no longer names `/claude-tweaks:flow {target} wrap-up` anywhere in that section — it names `/claude-tweaks:wrap-up {target} cleanup-only` instead.
9. A test confirms the status-line-before-artifact-check ordering per the Deliverables item above.
10. `tests/flow-cleanup-only-conformance.test.js`, `tests/build-already-shipped-exit.test.js`, `tests/dispatch-mechanical-enforcement.test.js`, `tests/dispatch-sequential-execution-conformance.test.js`, `tests/pr-first-merge.test.js`, and `tests/dispatch-settle-and-merge-lazy-read.test.js` all pass unchanged.

## Release Note

Dispatch now repairs and continues a build whose only problem is a missing run-configuration file, instead of abandoning a tested, correct pull request outside pipeline review.

## Technical Approach

The `repairable` field is additive and scoped to exactly one failure reason (`missing-config`), so no existing caller or test that checks other failure reasons is affected. The repair itself does no direct file writing — it relies on `/flow`'s own adoption case 3 (already-existing behavior, `steps-and-gates.md:72-80` and `preflight.js`'s `computeAdoption`) to rebuild `config.yml` through the sanctioned writer when call 2 runs. This unit's job is purely the classification (is a repair safe?) and the dispatch-side branch (route to repair instead of teardown).

### Data / API Surface

`checkFirstCallArtifacts`'s return shape gains one new optional field:

```
{ ok: boolean, reason?: string, repairable?: boolean, ...existingFields }
```

`repairable` is present only when `reason === 'missing-config'`; absent (not `false`) for every other `reason` value, and absent on `ok: true`.

### Key Files

- `plugin/bin/lib/dispatch/first-call-artifact-check.js` — add the continued-checks-on-missing-config logic and the `repairable` field; add a `repoRoot` (or equivalent injected `git`/`readFile` deps) the function currently lacks, needed to call `resolvePolicyConfig`.
- `plugin/bin/lib/policy-schema.js` (read-only) — `resolvePolicyConfig`/`resolvePolicyKeys` (the non-defaulting read, lines ~598-649 house this cluster) is the function this unit calls for `integration-model`; `resolveIntegrationModel` (same file) is the wrong function — it falls through to `detectIntegrationModel` and never fails, so it cannot produce the "policy read fails" signal AC 4 requires.
- `tests/bin-lib/dispatch/first-call-artifact-check.test.js` — add the five new cases listed in Acceptance Criteria.
- `plugin/skills/dispatch/two-call-gate.md` — §2: add the repair branch and its `AUTO` log-line template.
- `plugin/skills/dispatch/sequential-execution.md` — "The loop" (~line 30): mirror the repair branch; (~line 32): fix the stale teardown reference.
- `plugin/skills/flow/steps-and-gates.md` — read-only; confirms adoption case 3's definition (lines 72-80) that the repair branch relies on.
- `plugin/bin/lib/flow/preflight.js` — read-only; confirms `computeAdoption` returns case 3 for this run shape.

## Gotchas

- First-failure-wins is the existing, correct behavior for every failure reason other than `missing-config` — do not generalize the repair classification to other reasons; the design doc scopes it to this one case because it is the one case where the remaining evidence (claim, PR) can independently confirm the build is otherwise sound.
- A policy read failure must resolve `repairable: false`, never throw past the check or default to `true` — "never repair on missing evidence" is a stated design invariant, not an incidental default. Use `resolvePolicyConfig`/`resolvePolicyKeys`, not `resolveIntegrationModel` — the latter is documented to never fail (falls through to `detectIntegrationModel`'s own fail-open-to-`local-merge` default), so it cannot structurally produce the failure this AC requires.
- The #2429 status-line check still runs first in both `two-call-gate.md` and `sequential-execution.md` — a malformed status line is `BLOCKED` regardless of this unit's change; the repair branch is reachable only after that check and a `build-test-ok` pass on every other artifact-check dimension. This is now a tested invariant, not only a narrative one — see the Deliverables item and AC 9 above.
- `sequential-execution.md`'s stale `/claude-tweaks:flow {target} wrap-up` reference (~line 32) is a pre-existing bug this unit fixes in passing because it is in the same file section being edited for the repair branch — not a separate unrelated cleanup.
- The claim's own `runId` (not `config.yml`, which is absent on this path) is the comparison value for the "claim live and matching `runId`" check — the same claim record `checkFirstCallArtifacts` already reads for its existing claim checks on every other path.

Surface: infra

## Current State

`/claude-tweaks:build` tells every implementer, in fixed words, that "scratch checks stay scratch" (`plugin/skills/build/SKILL.md:223`, quoting CLAUDE.md's Working Approach). Nothing in build's plan guidance (`plugin/skills/build/plan-authoring-checks.md`) or its Final Verification step (`SKILL.md:266-272`, which runs `skills/test/verification.md`'s runner checks only) says what happens to the *result* of a scratch check. That matters when the check is the only evidence for an acceptance criterion. The plan is free to route that result into a conversational "build handoff" (`plugin/skills/build/handoff-template.md`).

That works in one session, but not under `/claude-tweaks:dispatch`'s two-call split. Call 1 (`build,test`) and call 2 (`review,polish,wrap-up`) are separate Task calls that share only the run directory. Review's spec-compliance check marks each criterion `met`/`partially met`/`not met` by asking whether it is "verifiable from the code and tests" (`plugin/skills/review/code-mode-steps.md:31`). It has no place to look for a scratch result call 1 produced.

Observed (original request below): an AC of "a rendered contrast audit over the main routes reports 0 failures" was met by a scratch audit in call 1. `decisions.md` mentioned "the AC2 rendered audit" with no result, counts, or log path, so call 2 had to re-run the whole audit (68 page renders plus controls).

`plugin/skills/build/SKILL.md` is 45,186 bytes against the 46,080-byte per-SKILL.md ceiling (`plugin/bin/lib/skill-audit/context-cost.js:31`, `45 * 1024`). New prose has to live in a sub-file.

## Deliverables

1. Add an "AC-evidence persistence" check to `plugin/skills/build/plan-authoring-checks.md`. When a plan task verifies an acceptance criterion only with a scratch (uncommitted) check, the plan must name that check's run-dir evidence destination, never a conversational handoff. The destination is one `decisions.md` entry written via `node "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/bin/log-decision.js" --run "$PIPELINE_RUN_DIR" --status AUTO --step "AC evidence"`. Its text carries:
   - the criterion it covers;
   - the exact command shape;
   - the pass/fail counts.
   When the check's output is too long for one line, the plan also writes the full log to `$PIPELINE_RUN_DIR/evidence/` and cites that path in the same entry.
2. In `plugin/skills/review/code-mode-steps.md`'s Acceptance Criteria check (check 2), add: before marking a criterion `not met` for lack of code or test evidence, read the run's `decisions.md` for an `AC evidence` entry naming it. When one exists, cite it as the criterion's evidence instead of re-executing the check. When `$PIPELINE_RUN_DIR` is unset (standalone review), behavior is unchanged.
3. Leave `plugin/skills/build/SKILL.md` unchanged. If a pointer is unavoidable, it must fit the ceiling headroom; confirm with `node plugin/bin/context-cost-report.js` or the context-cost test.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `plan-authoring-checks.md` carries a check requiring a scratch-verified AC's result to go to the run dir via `log-decision.js --step "AC evidence"`, with the criterion, command shape, and pass/fail counts in the entry text, plus a `$PIPELINE_RUN_DIR/evidence/` log for long output.
- `review/code-mode-steps.md`'s check 2 instructs reading `decisions.md` for an `AC evidence` entry and citing it rather than re-running the check. It names the unset-`$PIPELINE_RUN_DIR` standalone case as unchanged.
- `plugin/skills/build/SKILL.md` stays under the context-cost ceiling. The repo's context-cost test (`tests/bin-lib/skill-audit/context-cost.test.js`) passes.
- `npm test` passes, since conformance tests pin skill prose repo-wide.

## Release Note

Fix dispatched builds losing scratch-check results between calls: an acceptance criterion verified by an uncommitted check now leaves its result in the run directory for review to cite.

## Technical Approach

A prose-only change in two sub-files. The evidence channel reuses the existing sanctioned run-dir writer (`bin/log-decision.js`) rather than a new artifact format, so `/claude-tweaks:wrap-up`'s console and any later reader see it in the same `decisions.md` they already read. Write the `evidence/` subdirectory only for long logs, and keep its path under `$PIPELINE_RUN_DIR`, never a relative path, per `_shared/pipeline-run-dir.md`.

### Key Files

- `plugin/skills/build/plan-authoring-checks.md` — new AC-evidence persistence check
- `plugin/skills/review/code-mode-steps.md` — check 2 reads `AC evidence` entries before declaring a criterion unverified
- `plugin/skills/build/SKILL.md` — no change expected (ceiling headroom ~900 bytes)

## Gotchas

- "Scratch checks stay scratch" governs whether a check's *code* is committed, not whether its *result* is recorded. The new check must say so explicitly, so the two rules are not read as contradicting each other.
- A recorded result is evidence, not proof. Review may still re-run a check whose entry looks inconsistent with the diff, for example a stale command shape. The rule removes the forced re-run; it does not forbid one.
- Byte-pinned conformance tests cover `plugin/skills/**` prose. Run the full suite before merging, not just the targeted ones.

## Original request

build: an AC met only by a scratch check leaves no run-dir artifact for /dispatch's second call

**Summary:** An acceptance criterion met only by a scratch (uncommitted) check leaves no run-dir artifact, so /dispatch's second call cannot verify it without re-running the check.

**Kind:** Gap

**Affected component:** build (plan + test-phase exit), under /claude-tweaks:dispatch's two-call split

**Use case:**
A record's acceptance criterion read "a rendered contrast audit over the main routes reports 0 failures." The plan /build wrote said the audit "stays scratch (per the project's working approach); its result is reported in the build handoff." Under /dispatch's two-call split (`build,test`, then `review,polish,wrap-up` as a fresh Task call with no conversation), there is no conversational handoff. The first call's `decisions.md` mentioned "the AC2 rendered audit" but recorded no result, counts or log path. The second call's review has to re-derive its verdict from raw artifacts, so it had nothing to read for that criterion and had to re-run the whole audit (68 page renders plus controls).

Why was this possible? The plan routed the scratch check's result into a conversational handoff. Plans assume one session. Nothing in /build's plan or test-phase guidance says an AC verified only by an uncommitted check must persist its evidence to the run dir. CAUSAL: systemic.

Proposed fix: when an acceptance criterion's only evidence is a scratch check, /build's test-phase exit (or the plan template) should require one of two things:
- a `decisions.md` line carrying the result (pass/fail counts and the command shape), or
- the check's log written into the run dir.

The second dispatch call's review can then cite it as a raw artifact instead of re-running it or trusting a mention.

Acceptance: a dispatched two-call run whose AC is met by a scratch check leaves, in the run dir after call 1, a result line or log that call 2's review cites without re-executing the check.

**Definition:** Clear

**Plugin version:** 6.137.0

Surface: infra

## Current State

`liftMetadata` in `plugin/bin/lib/issues/materialize-format.js:119-138` lifts a record's body-metadata lines into the materialized header. The `Design-intent:` capture is `/^Design-intent:[ \t]*(\S+)/m` (`:131`). `\S+` stops at the first whitespace, so `Design-intent: quiet, minimal` lifts as `quiet,` (trailing comma kept, second value lost). `composeHeader` (`:157-169`) then writes `design-intent: quiet,` verbatim.

Multi-value intents are a supported shape downstream. `plugin/skills/design-wrapper/command-map.md:106` says "Multiple intents (comma-separated, e.g., `design-intent: bold, delightful`) trigger multiple dispatches." Polish reads the header's `design-intent:` for that dispatch, and so do `flow/manifesto.md:43` and `:57`. The run-level lever is a single-value enum in `plugin/bin/lib/policy-schema.js:95` (`none | bold | quiet | minimal | delightful | onboarding`).

In the reported run (plugin 6.136.0), the header read `design-intent: quiet,` and `config.yml` resolved to `quiet` only. Polish ran the `minimal` command only because the polish agent happened to re-read the record body. A mechanical header consumer would have skipped it.

## Deliverables

1. Change `liftMetadata`'s `Design-intent:` capture to the full same-line value: split on `,`, trim each value, drop empties, and validate each against the closed enum from `policy-schema.js:95` (read from there, not re-listed). The lifted value is a normalized list.
2. `composeHeader` writes the normalized list as `design-intent: quiet, minimal` (comma plus single space), the shape `command-map.md:106` documents. A single value is written exactly as today.
3. An unknown value (outside the enum), or a list that mixes `none` with any other value, fails materialization with a message naming the record and the offending value, the same hard-gate posture as other malformed header input. It never silently drops the value.
4. Decide how a multi-value header maps to the run-level `design-intent` lever, which is single-valued in `policy-schema.js`. Either have polish read the header list (not the lever) for dispatch, or document in `flow/manifesto.md` that the lever is a run default and the header list is authoritative per record. Pick one, and make the manifesto's Design-intent row (`manifesto.md:57`) state it.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A unit test lifts `Design-intent: quiet, minimal` and asserts the header line `design-intent: quiet, minimal`. Prove it goes red against the current `\S+` capture.
- Unit tests cover: a single value (unchanged output); extra spaces and a trailing comma (`quiet ,minimal,` → `quiet, minimal`); an unknown value (materialization fails, naming it); `none, bold` (fails).
- A bare `Design-intent:` line with no value still lifts nothing. The existing refs-#357 same-line-only behavior is pinned by an unchanged test.
- The polish dispatch path receives both intents for a two-value header, asserted by a test or conformance check on whichever consumer Deliverable 4 picks.
- `npm test` passes in full.

## Release Note

Records with more than one design intent now carry every intent into the build, so polish runs each one instead of only the first.

## Technical Approach

Keep the change local to `liftMetadata`/`composeHeader`. Capture with `(.+)$` like `Ui-stack:` already does at `:133`, keeping the `[ \t]*` same-line guard, then normalize. Source the enum from `policy-schema.js` so the two cannot drift. Hard-fail on invalid values rather than filtering: a silent drop is the exact failure this record reports, one level down.

### Key Files

- `plugin/bin/lib/issues/materialize-format.js` — `liftMetadata` `Design-intent:` capture (`:131-132`), list normalization and validation; `composeHeader` output (`:169`)
- `plugin/bin/lib/policy-schema.js` — enum source of truth (`:95`), read not modified
- `plugin/skills/flow/manifesto.md` — Design-intent lever vs. per-record header list (`:43`, `:57`)
- `plugin/skills/design-wrapper/command-map.md` — reference for the documented multi-intent shape (`:106`)

## Gotchas

- The refs-#357 comment at `materialize-format.js:124-128` explains why every capture uses `[ \t]*`, not `\s*`. Keep that guard on the new capture, or a bare `Design-intent:` line will swallow the next line.
- `yamlSafeScalar` (`:146`) is applied only to `ui-stack`. A comma-separated list contains no `:` or `#`, so it needs no quoting, but do not route it through a YAML-list syntax that other header readers do not parse.
- Records already materialized with `design-intent: quiet,` live in old run dirs. Readers must not crash on that legacy shape. Treat a trailing comma as a trimmed list on read too, if any reader re-parses the header.

## Original request

materialize.js: a comma-separated `Design-intent:` list is truncated to its first value

**Summary:** `materialize.js` lifts `Design-intent: quiet, minimal` into the materialized header as `design-intent: quiet,` — trailing comma kept, second value lost.

**Kind:** Defect

**Affected component:** bin/materialize.js, bin/lib/issues/materialize-format.js (`liftMetadata`)

**Repro steps:**
1. Create a record whose body carries `Design-intent: quiet, minimal` (what `/claude-tweaks:specify` writes when two intents are picked).
2. Run `/claude-tweaks:flow #N` (or `bin/materialize.js` directly) to materialize it.
3. Read the materialized header in `{run-dir}/work/{n}-spec.md` and the run's `config.yml` `design-intent` lever.

**Expected vs. actual:**
Expected: the whole list is lifted (`design-intent: quiet, minimal`, or a YAML list), or each value is validated against the closed enum (`bold | quiet | minimal | delightful | onboarding | none`) and malformed input fails the materialization gate.
Actual: the header reads `design-intent: quiet,` and `config.yml` resolves to `quiet` only. The polish phase still ran the `minimal` intent's command only because the polish agent re-read the record body; a mechanical consumer of the header would have skipped it.

Suggested fix: capture the full same-line value, split on `,`, trim, validate against the enum, emit a normalized list; add a test for a two-value intent line.

**Definition:** Clear

**Plugin version:** 6.136.0

Surface: infra

**Related:** #2775, #2783, #2868, #2912, #2914, #2994, #3003, #3012, #3132

## Current State

When `/claude-tweaks:flow` adopts an inherited run directory, as `/claude-tweaks:dispatch`'s second call (`review,polish,wrap-up`) does, it gathers facts once via `bin/flow-preflight.js` (`plugin/skills/flow/steps-and-gates.md:56-60`). The pack's `pr` probe (`plugin/bin/lib/flow/preflight.js:263-268`) runs `gh pr view {n} --json state,isDraft,body` and returns `{number, url, branch, state, isDraft, checklist}`. It never reads `mergeable` or `mergeStateStatus`.

In the reported run (plugin 6.136.0), the integration branch moved between the two dispatch calls. A sibling PR edited the same two lines of two skill docs, so the run's PR became `CONFLICTING`. GitHub runs no `pull_request` CI on a conflicting PR, so the checks list held only the label workflow. The second call's verification stamp and the first call's decisions log both read green. The conflict surfaced only because the reviewer ran an ad-hoc `gh pr view --json mergeable`. Nothing in the pack, the adoption path, or `/review` Step 1.5 (`plugin/skills/review/code-mode-steps.md:57`) looks at mergeability.

## Deliverables

1. Extend the pack's `pr` probe to request `mergeable,mergeStateStatus` alongside `state,isDraft,body`, and return both fields. A forge or `gh` that omits them yields `null` for that field, never an error that fails the whole `pr` probe.
2. On the adopted-run path (`steps-and-gates.md`'s "Adopting an inherited run directory"), when the pack's `pr.mergeable` is `CONFLICTING`, print one visible line before any later phase runs: `Run PR #{n} is CONFLICTING with {integration branch} — CI will not run on it until the conflict is resolved.` Log it as an `AUTO` decision. Then reconcile per the existing catch-up procedure: merge the integration branch into the run branch, then re-verify. This is the same remedy `_shared/worktree-catchup-no-run-dir.md` and the phase-exit pushes already use. Cite the existing procedure; do not restate it.
3. When the merge in deliverable 2 itself conflicts, stop as a HARD-GATE failure with the conflicting paths named, rather than continuing to review on a stamp that no longer describes a mergeable tree.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A unit test feeds the `pr` probe a `gh` stub returning `mergeable: CONFLICTING` and asserts the pack's `pr` carries `mergeable` and `mergeStateStatus`. A stub omitting both asserts `null` values and `ok: true`.
- A test or conformance assertion pins the adopted-run path's `CONFLICTING` line and its routing to the catch-up procedure. It goes red against the current `steps-and-gates.md`.
- A `MERGEABLE` or `UNKNOWN` PR produces no new line, no new decision entry, and no behavior change. A test asserts this.
- Existing `tests/bin-lib/flow/preflight.test.js`, `tests/bin-lib/flow/preflight-cli.test.js`, and `tests/flow-preflight-conformance.test.js` pass, updated only where they pin the `pr` field's exact key set.
- `npm test` passes in full.

## Release Note

A resumed pipeline run now notices when its pull request has picked up a merge conflict since the last call, and catches up before reviewing.

## Technical Approach

Keep the change inside the probe that already reads the PR. One more pair of JSON fields on the same `gh pr view` call adds no new network round-trip. The adoption-path handling is prose in `steps-and-gates.md`, keyed off the pack field, so the decision stays mechanical and is never re-derived by hand. `UNKNOWN` is GitHub's transient value while it computes mergeability, so it must stay a no-op, as the original request asks. The merge gate re-reads mergeability at merge time anyway.

### Key Files

- `plugin/bin/lib/flow/preflight.js` — `pr` probe (`:263-268`) requests and returns `mergeable`/`mergeStateStatus`
- `plugin/skills/flow/steps-and-gates.md` — "Adopting an inherited run directory" (`:56`) surfaces a `CONFLICTING` PR and routes to catch-up
- `tests/bin-lib/flow/preflight.test.js` — `pr` probe field assertions
- `tests/flow-preflight-conformance.test.js` — adoption-path prose pin

## Gotchas

- The pack field set may be pinned by conformance tests and consumed by other readers of `preflight.json`. Add fields; never rename or drop `state`/`isDraft`/`checklist`.
- `mergeable` is computed lazily by GitHub. A first read right after a push often returns `UNKNOWN`. Do not poll in the probe, because the pack has a probe timeout (`PROBE_TIMEOUT_MS`, `preflight.js:284`).
- #3013 (ready) adds a PR-check read to `/test` and `/review` Step 1.5. A conflicting PR has no CI, so an empty check rollup there would read as pending. These two records cover different signals. Keep the `CONFLICTING` handling on the adoption path, as this record specifies, and do not fold it into #3013's check read.

## Original request

flow-preflight's pr probe omits mergeable state, so a two-call dispatch resume misses a PR that turned CONFLICTING between calls

**Kind:** Gap

**Affected component:** bin/flow-preflight.js (pr probe), skills/flow/steps-and-gates.md (Adopting an inherited run directory)

## Current State

On a `/claude-tweaks:dispatch` two-call handoff (`build,test`, then `review,polish,wrap-up` against the same `PIPELINE_RUN_DIR`), the second call's `flow-preflight.js` pack reports `pr: {number, url, branch, state, isDraft, checklist}`. It does not report `mergeable`. In one run the integration branch moved between the two calls. A sibling PR edited the same two lines of two skill docs, so the run's PR was `CONFLICTING`. The forge then ran no `pull_request` CI on it (GitHub skips CI on conflicting PRs). The second call's verification stamp and the first call's decisions log both read green. The conflict surfaced only because the reviewer ran an ad-hoc `gh pr view --json mergeable` and found just the label workflow in the checks list. Nothing in the pack or in review Step 1.5/2 checks it.

## Deliverables

- Add `mergeable` (and `mergeStateStatus` where the forge supports it) to the pack's `pr` probe.
- When it reads `CONFLICTING`, surface it on the adopted-run path, before review's test gate trusts a stamp. Either say how to reconcile (merge the integration branch in, then re-verify) or make it an explicit gate.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A resumed run whose PR is `CONFLICTING` prints a visible line naming the conflict before review starts.
- A `MERGEABLE` or `UNKNOWN` PR changes nothing.

**Definition:** Clear

Surface: infra

## Current State

`/claude-tweaks:build`'s default execution strategy invokes `/superpowers:subagent-driven-development` (`plugin/skills/build/build-options.md:11`, invocation instructions in `plugin/skills/build/dispatch.md:14`). SDD runs a reviewer per task and a whole-branch review at the end, and both can return Minor findings. `/build` never says what happens to those findings. No file under `plugin/skills/build/` cites `_shared/deferral-gate.md`, so the build agent improvises its ledger writes. The ledger's only build-time entry rule is Common Step 4 (`build/SKILL.md:244-252`), which covers blocked work: "Append blocked items to the open items ledger ... with phase `build/*` and status `open`".

`_shared/deferral-gate.md:27` requires a ledger entry that recommends deferral to pass the same fix-now check and name its `Defer-reason:` inline. `:39` lists "Minor / outside that scope / not load-bearing" as a bad reason, since severity is never a defer reason. `_shared/ledger-format.md:59` additionally requires `deferred` resolution text to carry origin, affected files and a revisit trigger.

In the reported run (plugin 6.136.0), the build wrote review minors as `deferred | SDD minor (deferred), triaged fine-to-defer by the whole-branch review.` or `open | —`. Six of the eleven carried rows qualified for fix-now: a number-format call, two missing unit assertions, an indentation fix, a missing e2e fixture, a live-region condition and a design-doc note. The deferral gate first ran on them at the later call's review, which cost an extra fix wave and two scoped verification runs after the build's final verification had already passed.

## Deliverables

1. In `build/dispatch.md`'s SDD invocation instruction, add a rule for review findings: every Minor (or higher) finding from a per-task reviewer or the whole-branch review is either fixed in this build, or carried to the ledger only after passing `_shared/deferral-gate.md`'s fix-now check with exactly one `Defer-reason:` from that file's vocabulary, written inline in the row's Resolution text. Severity alone ("minor", "fine to defer") is never a reason. Cite the gate file rather than restating its criteria.
2. Add the same rule to `build/SKILL.md`'s Common Step 4, next to the blocked-work ledger instruction, so the ledger-write site names the gate whatever execution strategy ran (subagent or inline).
3. Make the gap visible mechanically: when the open-items ledger carries a `build/*`-phase row whose status is `deferred` or `open` and whose Resolution text has no valid `Defer-reason:` value, the wrap-up fact pack's ledger parse reports it. Surface it at wrap-up as a non-blocking warning naming the rows, mirroring the unrecognized-status warning (`wrap-up/SKILL.md:208`, `ledger-format.md:57`, `parseLedger` in `plugin/bin/lib/wrap-up/pack.js`). Reuse `DEFER_REASONS` from `plugin/bin/lib/issues/autonomy.js` for validity.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `build/dispatch.md` and `build/SKILL.md` both cite `_shared/deferral-gate.md` at the review-finding / ledger-write instruction. A conformance test pins both citations and the "severity is never a reason" wording, and goes red against the current text.
- A unit test feeds `parseLedger` a ledger with three `build/*` rows: one `deferred` with a valid `Defer-reason:`, one `deferred` with "SDD minor (deferred)", and one `open | —`. It asserts that exactly the last two are reported as missing a defer reason.
- The wrap-up warning names the rows and never blocks. An existing wrap-up/ledger test passes unchanged.
- `npm test` passes in full.

## Release Note

Build no longer parks minor review findings in the open-items ledger without a valid defer reason. It fixes them or names why they can wait.

## Technical Approach

The prose fix is two citations of the existing gate, at the SDD invocation and at the ledger-write step. The mechanical backstop sits in the ledger parse that wrap-up already runs, reusing the closed `DEFER_REASONS` vocabulary, so a build that ignores the prose still gets caught before the end-of-run console rather than one call later at review.

### Key Files

- `plugin/skills/build/dispatch.md` — SDD invocation instruction gains the review-finding deferral rule
- `plugin/skills/build/SKILL.md` — Common Step 4 cites `_shared/deferral-gate.md` for review findings carried to the ledger
- `plugin/bin/lib/wrap-up/pack.js` — `parseLedger` reports `build/*` deferred/open rows lacking a valid `Defer-reason:`
- `plugin/bin/lib/issues/autonomy.js` — reference only: `DEFER_REASONS` source of truth
- `plugin/skills/wrap-up/SKILL.md` — surfaces the new non-blocking warning next to the out-of-enum status warning

## Gotchas

- Blocked-work rows (Common Step 4's original purpose) are `open` by design until the ledger resolve gate runs. The backstop must not flag a genuinely blocked row. Scope the check to rows that recommend deferral, or require blocked rows to name `Defer-reason: blocked-dependency` or `blocked-external` as well. Pick one and state it in the PR.
- SDD is a third-party skill (superpowers). The instruction has to travel in `/build`'s invocation text. Do not edit the upstream skill.
- `parseLedger` is at `plugin/bin/lib/wrap-up/pack.js:332`. Check that its row shape carries phase and Resolution text before extending it, and add fields rather than changing existing ones, since the Resolve Gate and the unrecognized-status warning (`wrap-up/SKILL.md:208`) already consume it.

## Original request

build: review minors are carried into the ledger as deferred with no Defer-reason

**Summary:** `/build`'s subagent-driven review triage wrote minor findings into the open-items ledger as `deferred` ("fine to defer") or left them `open`, with no `Defer-reason:` and no fix-now attempt, so the deferral gate ran on them for the first time at wrap-up.

**Kind:** Defect

**Affected component:** `/claude-tweaks:build` (the review rulings' ledger writes) against `_shared/deferral-gate.md`

**Repro steps:**
1. Build a record whose whole-branch review returns Minor findings it triages as "fine to defer".
2. Read the open-items ledger after the build: the rows read `deferred | SDD minor (deferred), triaged fine-to-defer by the whole-branch review.` or `open | —`.
3. Run review and wrap-up in a later call.

**Expected vs. actual:**
Expected: per `_shared/deferral-gate.md` ("A ledger entry recommending deferral runs this same check, even in prose"), each such row is either fixed at build time or names exactly one `Defer-reason:` from the closed vocabulary; "minor" is listed there as a bad reason to skip a fix.
Actual: six of the eleven carried rows had no valid reason and qualified for fix-now (a number-format call, two missing unit assertions, an indentation fix, a missing e2e fixture, a live-region condition, a design-doc note). They were fixed during the later call's review instead, which cost an extra fix wave and two scoped verification runs after the build's own final verification had already passed.

**Definition:** Clear

Surface: infra

## Current State

`ledgerProbe` in `plugin/bin/lib/wrap-up/pack.js:366-418` reads `{run-dir}/ledger.md` first. When that file is absent, it falls back to every `*-ledger.md` under `{worktree}/docs/plans/` (`:378-379`) and picks among them with two heuristics:

- **Exactly one candidate**: the probe treats it as "unambiguously this run's" (`:380-388`), without checking.
- **Two or more candidates, none naming one of this run's records at a `-{n}-`/`-{n}.` boundary** (`namesRecord`, `:362-364`): the probe counts **every** candidate (`:396`), deliberately failing toward over-counting (#2563).

Both heuristics assume the only ledgers in `docs/plans/` are this run's own. That is false in this repo. Finished runs' ledgers stay committed on `main` (for example `docs/plans/2026-10-03-record-2853-ledger.md` and `docs/plans/2026-10-04-record-2772-ledger.md` are tracked today), so every new worktree branched from `main` inherits them. A run that never created its own docs/plans ledger therefore gets either a stranger's ledger counted as its own (one candidate) or all the strangers' ledgers summed (several candidates). This is what happened on #2852's wrap-up: `pack.ledger` reported an unrelated, still-active run's ledger.

## Deliverables

1. Attribute ledgers to the run by ownership, not by filename heuristics. Treat a `docs/plans/*-ledger.md` as this run's only when this run's branch added or modified it relative to its merge base. Keep `namesRecord` only as a secondary tie-break among owned candidates.
2. When no candidate is owned by this run, report zero items. Also expose the unattributed candidates in a distinct field (for example `unattributedFiles`) so a human can still see them. Never sum them into `open` or `total`.
3. Update `pack.test.js` with cases for: one inherited (unowned) ledger, several inherited ledgers with none owned, one owned ledger alongside inherited ones, and the `{run-dir}/ledger.md` precedence (unchanged).

## Acceptance Criteria

- A worktree whose `docs/plans/` holds only ledgers inherited from the merge base gets `pack.ledger` with `open: 0`, `total: 0`, and those files listed under the unattributed field, not under `files`.
- A worktree with one ledger added on its branch plus inherited ledgers counts only the added ledger's items.
- `{run-dir}/ledger.md`, when present, still takes precedence with unchanged output.
- `npm test` passes in full.

## Release Note

Fixed wrap-up counting open items from other runs' ledger files as if they belonged to the current run.

## Technical Approach

The probe already runs where a base ref is available: wrap-up's pack has the run's integration branch and merge base for its other probes. Derive owned files with `git diff --name-only {merge-base}...HEAD -- docs/plans/` through the probe's injectable `deps` seam, so the tests stay hermetic. Keep the existing #2563 rationale in mind. The over-count fallback existed because the only alternative was silently hiding the run's own items, and ownership-by-diff removes that dilemma. Update the comment block at `:380-396` to match.

### Key Files

- `plugin/bin/lib/wrap-up/pack.js` — `ledgerProbe` (366-418): ownership-based attribution plus an unattributed field
- `tests/bin-lib/wrap-up/pack.test.js` — inherited/owned ledger cases
- `plugin/skills/_shared/ledger-format.md` — read-only check: its Location section's "one ledger per pipeline run" wording should still hold after the change

## Gotchas

- A run whose ledger was created and committed earlier on the same branch still counts as owned, because the merge-base diff includes it. A ledger that only exists uncommitted in the worktree also needs handling. Include untracked or modified files from `git status --porcelain -- docs/plans/` along with the diff.
- Any consumer that reads `pack.ledger.files` (wrap-up's resolve gate, the Review Console) must not start treating the new unattributed field as blocking. Grep for `ledger.files` and `pack.ledger` consumers before changing the shape.
- The accumulation of finished runs' ledgers on `main` is itself a separate cleanup question. It is out of scope here, and the probe must be correct regardless.

## Original request

wrap-up-pack.js's ledger probe can match an unrelated run's ledger file

Origin: wrap-up (#2852)
Defer-reason: pre-existing-outside-diff

**Related:** none

Context: wrap-up's ledger probe (bin/lib/wrap-up/pack.js) falls back to a bare docs/plans/*-ledger.md glob when a run has no run-dir ledger.md. On #2852's wrap-up it matched an unrelated, still-active run's shared ledger instead of reporting none.

Scope: Scope the fallback to this run's own feature-slug, or verify the match actually belongs to this run, before reporting it as pack.ledger.

Surface: infra

**Related:** #3044 (item 1 of the original request — the AC-forwarding sample's sanctioned writer — is already its own `ready` record; out of scope here)

## Current State

The original report bundles four friction points from one `/flow` run on 6.132.0 (Windows, worktree-isolated). Checked against this tree:

1. **AC-forwarding sample path unwritable from a worktree session** — already shaped as #3044, which covers exactly this. Excluded from this record.
2. **`computeDiffFacts` input shape vs its documented call — confirmed.** `plugin/skills/build/dispatch.md:19` says to compute diff facts "via `bin/lib/dispatch/ceremony-derive.js`'s `computeDiffFacts` over the branch's `git diff --numstat` output". `plugin/skills/wrap-up/ceremony-derivation.md:30` uses the same phrasing. But `computeDiffFacts(files)` (`plugin/bin/lib/dispatch/ceremony-derive.js:25-29`) takes the parsed `[{path, additions, deletions}]` array, which `parseNumstat` produces. `parseNumstat` is exported from `plugin/bin/lib/blast-radius-cli.js:40,145`. Neither doc names the parser, so following the prose literally passes a raw string and throws.
3. **Circular-dependency warnings on the documented security-hardening invocation — confirmed, but the false-clean claim is not reproduced.** Running `plugin/skills/review/focus-criterion-passes.md:12`'s direct `require` of `candidates-security-hardening.js` emits `Accessing non-existent property 'listTrackedSourceFiles' … inside circular dependency`, along with the same warning for `isGlobDiscoveredTestFile`, `extractModuleExports`, `escapeRegExp` and `listTrackedFiles`. The cause is require order. `candidates-security-hardening.js:143-144` requires `./candidates-dead-code` before `./focus-generators`. `candidates-experiment-cleanup.js:60-61` does the same and also emits warnings when required directly. The ordering rule documented at `candidates-abstraction-police.js:56-68` says to require the registry first, because otherwise Node hands a sibling generator a partially loaded `candidates-dead-code` exports object and its helpers bind to `undefined`. On this repo, `scanSecurityHardening(process.cwd())` still returns a non-empty `{candidates: [...]}`. The scan itself therefore works here, and the generator actually affected by the half-loaded exports is `candidates-abstraction-police.js` in that same process.
4. **`log-decision.js --reversibility` rejects the documented qualifier form — confirmed.** `plugin/bin/log-decision.js:51` accepts only `high|med|low|n/a`. Meanwhile `plugin/skills/_shared/pr-early-run-lifecycle.md:154,307,333` mandates log lines such as `Reversibility: high (branch can be reset/force-pushed).`, and `plugin/bin/lib/log-decision/append.js:51` renders `Reversibility: ${reversibility}.`. The sanctioned writer cannot produce the documented line.

## Deliverables

1. **Item 2:** in `build/dispatch.md:19` and `wrap-up/ceremony-derivation.md:30`, state that the numstat output is parsed with `parseNumstat` (`bin/lib/blast-radius-cli.js`) before `computeDiffFacts` is called. Give a one-line runnable `node -e` composing the two.
2. **Item 3:** fix the require order in `candidates-security-hardening.js` and `candidates-experiment-cleanup.js` so `./focus-generators` is required before `./candidates-dead-code`, matching `candidates-abstraction-police.js`'s documented rule. Add a regression test: requiring each `candidates-*.js` module directly in a fresh `node` process emits no `inside circular dependency` warning.
3. **Item 4:** make `log-decision.js --reversibility` accept a tier with a trailing parenthetical qualifier (`high (branch can be reset/force-pushed)`). Validate the tier against the existing enum and render the qualifier verbatim, so the written line matches `pr-early-run-lifecycle.md`'s mandated form. A bare tier keeps working unchanged. Check that `claim-log.js`'s `ACTION_RE` (`plugin/bin/lib/log-decision/claim-log.js:23`) still parses lines that carry a qualifier.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `build/dispatch.md` and `wrap-up/ceremony-derivation.md` name `parseNumstat` as the step between `git diff --numstat` and `computeDiffFacts`.
- `node -e "require('./plugin/bin/lib/code-health/candidates-security-hardening.js')" 2>&1 | grep -c "circular dependency"` prints `0`, and the same holds for every other `candidates-*.js` module. A test pins this.
- `log-decision.js --reversibility "high (branch can be reset/force-pushed)"` exits 0 and writes `Reversibility: high (branch can be reset/force-pushed).`. `--reversibility "bogus (x)"` still exits non-zero. Tests cover both cases.
- `npm test` passes in full.

## Release Note

Fixed misleading circular-dependency warnings from code-health scanners and let the decision logger record reversibility notes the pipeline docs require.

## Technical Approach

The three items are independent, small, and touch disjoint files, so build them as three separate commits. Item 3: swap the two require lines in each offending module. The warning test spawns `node -e "require(...)"` per module and asserts that stderr contains no `circular dependency` string. Item 4: parse `^(high|med|low|n/a)(\s+\(.+\))?$`, validate group 1 against `REVERSIBILITY`, and pass the full string through to `formatEntry`. Item 2 is prose only.

### Key Files

- `plugin/skills/build/dispatch.md` — name `parseNumstat` before `computeDiffFacts` (line 19)
- `plugin/skills/wrap-up/ceremony-derivation.md` — same correction (line 30)
- `plugin/bin/lib/code-health/candidates-security-hardening.js` — require `./focus-generators` before `./candidates-dead-code`
- `plugin/bin/lib/code-health/candidates-experiment-cleanup.js` — same require-order fix
- `plugin/bin/log-decision.js` — accept a tier with a trailing parenthetical qualifier
- `plugin/bin/lib/log-decision/append.js` — render the qualifier verbatim
- `plugin/bin/lib/log-decision/claim-log.js` — confirm `ACTION_RE` tolerates a qualifier
- `tests/bin-lib/code-health/candidates-security-hardening.test.js` — add the no-circular-warning assertion (or a sibling test covering every `candidates-*.js`)

## Gotchas

- ASSUMPTION — verify at build: the reporter's `[]` result from `scanSecurityHardening` on their own repo was a legitimate zero-match rather than a cycle-induced false clean. It was not reproduced here (the scan returns candidates on this repo), and this run's return shape (`{candidates}`) differs from the array the reporter saw on 6.132.0. Confirm by running the scan against a fixture containing an `api/` route with a known finding, both before and after the require-order fix.
- Do not fix item 3 by suppressing Node warnings. The undefined bindings are real for whichever generator loads mid-cycle.
- Item 1 belongs to #3044. Do not fold a sample-file writer into this record.

## Original request

Four friction points in a /flow build-review-wrap-up run under worktree isolation (claude-tweaks 6.132.0)

Component: claude-tweaks plugin (skills/build/dispatch.md, bin/lib/dispatch/ceremony-derive.js, bin/lib/code-health/candidates-security-hardening.js, bin/log-decision.js)
Kind: defect

## Summary

A single-record `/claude-tweaks:flow` run (worktree-isolated session, Windows, plugin 6.132.0) hit four plugin-side issues. Item 3 is the most important: it looks like a silent false-clean in review's Step 6.6 security-hardening pass.

## 1. `build/dispatch.md`'s AC-forwarding sample path is unwritable from a worktree session

`skills/build/dispatch.md` ("Standing AC-forwarding verification") tells the run to copy the first reviewer prompt to `$PIPELINE_RUN_DIR/sdd-dispatch-sample.txt`. In a worktree-isolated session the harness's Write tool refuses that path ("Edit the worktree copy of this file instead of the shared-checkout path"), because the run dir is anchored in the main checkout. Workaround used: write inside the worktree, then `cp`. Suggest: document a sanctioned writer (as for `log-decision.js`/`stage-item.js`), or name a worktree-local sample path.

## 2. `computeDiffFacts` input shape vs. its documented call

`skills/build/dispatch.md` ("Whole-branch review model") says to compute diff facts "via `bin/lib/dispatch/ceremony-derive.js`'s `computeDiffFacts` over the branch's `git diff --numstat` output". The function expects the parsed `{path, additions, deletions}[]` array (`blast-radius-cli.js`'s `parseNumstat` shape). Running review Step 6.6's documented invocation:

```
node -e "const {scanSecurityHardening}=require('<plugin>/bin/lib/code-health/candidates-security-hardening.js'); console.log(JSON.stringify(scanSecurityHardening(process.cwd())))"
```

`_shared/pr-early-run-lifecycle.md`'s mandatory log lines read e.g. `Reversibility: high (branch can be reset/force-pushed).` Passing that as `--reversibility "high (branch can be reset/force-pushed)"` fails: `--reversibility must be one of high|med|low|n/a`. claude-tweaks 6.132.0; Claude Code on Windows 11, Git Bash; worktree-isolated session (`worktree-always` policy).

Surface: infra

## Current State

`manifesto.md`'s lever table states `merge-authorization`'s default is always `ask`, and explicitly: "Never a `policy.yml` default — only a live `confirm`/`hybrid` override sets it." This means a default `auto`-mode `/flow` invocation (the documented common case — "the everyday run has effectively one user-facing stop") can never pre-authorize its own merge, regardless of how high the project's resolved `autonomy` ceiling is (`_shared/autonomy-ceiling.md`) — even at `unattended`, which already raises `review-auto-apply-ceiling` to `medium` and grants `consoleAutoResolve` for other bookkeeping.

In this session, the project's autonomy ceiling resolved to `unattended` for both `/flow` runs, yet the Wrap-Up Review Console's merge-approval question still required a live click each time. The second run's merge-approval `AskUserQuestion` sat unanswered for roughly 7.5 hours (the large majority of this session's ~8.6-hour wall-clock span) before the user answered — and when they did, it matched the pre-marked Recommended option, the same as all 3 of this session's `AskUserQuestion` stops (3-for-3 Recommended).

This is a real cost: a project that has already opted into `unattended` operation (accepting that ledger bookkeeping, queue writes, and ops-acks resolve without a click) still can't finish a fully green, tested, reviewed run without a human present to click one more button — turning what the project's own policy says should be hands-off into a multi-hour stall whenever nobody happens to be watching.

**Existing mechanism, found during shaping.** `_shared/autonomy-ceiling.md` already documents a *per-run* escape hatch, distinct from `consoleAutoResolve`: an explicit Manifesto `confirm`/`hybrid` override can set `merge-authorization` for that one run — "always requiring a live answer... regardless of the project's ceiling setting," never settable via `policy.yml`. The same passage states plainly: "an `unattended`-ceiling project still needs `consoleAutoResolve` (or this lever) to actually skip the terminal click — raising the ceiling alone does not, by itself, answer this lever." This confirms the gap precisely: `consoleAutoResolve` is granted automatically at `unattended` and resolves every *other* Review Console section with zero clicks, but `merge-authorization`'s `ask` default is either a deliberate carve-out `consoleAutoResolve` does not override, or (less likely, given how explicitly this is documented) a genuine implementation gap — Deliverable 1 below needs to settle which, since the doc reads as intentional design, not an oversight, but the actual session cost (a 7.5h stall) argues the design should be revisited regardless of original intent.

## Deliverables

- [ ] Decide whether a sufficiently high resolved `autonomy` ceiling (e.g. `unattended` + `consoleAutoResolve` granted) should be allowed to extend to `merge-authorization` directly — i.e., add this as a new bookkeeping capability alongside the ones `_shared/autonomy-ceiling.md` already lets `unattended` resolve without a click — or keep merge-authorization permanently `confirm`/`hybrid`-only by design (in which case, document explicitly why merge is excluded from every other `unattended` bookkeeping capability, so this isn't re-discovered as a fresh gap later).
- [ ] If extending: implement the new capability path in `_shared/autonomy-ceiling.md`'s `bookkeepingPermissions()` and thread it through `manifesto.md`'s lever-default computation and the Review Console's terminal-decision resolution.
- [ ] Alternative middle ground, if full extension seems too broad: a lightweight one-time opt-in flag on the `/flow` command line itself (distinct from `confirm`/`hybrid` mode, which reopens the whole Manifesto gate) that pre-authorizes just this run's merge — sparing a `confirm`-mode user from re-litigating every other lever just to unlock hands-off merge.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A documented decision exists for whether/how `unattended` extends to merge-authorization.
2. If implemented, a default-`auto` `/flow` run at `unattended` with `consoleAutoResolve` granted completes end-to-end (merge included) with zero required clicks, matching the behavior already true for every other bookkeeping capability at that ceiling.
3. `npm test` passes.

## Technical Approach

Whichever way Deliverable 1 resolves, the change site is `bin/lib/issues/autonomy.js`'s `bookkeepingPermissions(ceiling)` (the single source of truth `_shared/autonomy-ceiling.md`'s Bookkeeping capabilities table documents) plus `manifesto.md`'s lever-default computation and the Review Console's terminal-decision resolution path — the same three places every existing `unattended`-only capability (`opsAckAutoAcknowledge`, `consoleAutoResolve`, `refineAutoApply`, `ledgerRouteRemainder`) already threads through, so a new `mergeAuthorizationAutoResolve`-shaped capability (if the decision favors extension) follows the identical pattern rather than inventing a new mechanism. If the decision instead favors the command-line opt-in flag (Deliverable 3's middle ground), that's a `/flow` argument-parsing change plus a one-line Manifesto lever override, independent of the `bookkeepingPermissions()` table.

### Key Files

- `plugin/skills/flow/manifesto.md` — the `merge-authorization: ask` default (line ~181) and the "Never a `policy.yml` default" rule
- `plugin/skills/_shared/autonomy-ceiling.md` — `bookkeepingPermissions()`'s documented table, and the existing per-run confirm/hybrid override this record's investigation found (the "this lever" passage) — the natural place to add a new capability row if the decision favors extension
- `plugin/bin/lib/issues/autonomy.js` — `bookkeepingPermissions(ceiling)`'s actual code, the source of truth the markdown table documents

## Gotchas

- The existing confirm/hybrid per-run override is a real, already-working mechanism for pre-authorizing one run's merge — don't present this record as "there's no way to do this today" in a build; the gap is specifically that `auto` mode + `unattended` ceiling can't reach the same outcome without reopening the whole Manifesto gate.
- `_shared/autonomy-ceiling.md`'s own prose reads like the current `ask`-always default for merge-authorization was a deliberate, considered design choice (it's called out explicitly, not silently absent) — treat "was this intentional" as a real open question for Deliverable 1, not an assumed bug, even though the session cost (7.5h stall) argues for revisiting it.

## Current State

`verify.js --baseline` (#3043) classifies a failing test file as `baseline-flaky` when it fails in the full run but passes when re-run alone at HEAD, and prints one `CAVEAT: baseline-flaky:` line. The verdict goes nowhere else:
- It is never counted into the count stamp's `flakyHits`. That is the counter #1925's allowlisted retry feeds, and it drives the five-hit `flaky-allowlist` escalation caveat.
- It never stages a proposal to add the file to `.claude-tweaks/verify-scope.json`'s `flaky.files`.

A file that keeps passing only in isolation is therefore invisible beyond each run's own CAVEAT.

Evidence: #3043's final whole-branch review follow-up I3 (ledger row 17). In the live runs, `tests/bin-lib/gif/palette.test.js`, `tests/bin-lib/hooks/reconcile-background.test.js` and `tests/bin-lib/file-lock.test.js` each landed as baseline-flaky.

## Deliverables

- [ ] Count every `baselineAdjudicated.flakyPassed` file into `flakyHits` exactly as a retried allowlisted file is counted, in the count stamp's existing shape.
- [ ] A file whose hits reach the escalation threshold without being on `flaky.files` stages a `flaky-allowlist` proposal for the Review Console. It is never applied silently.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] After two adjudicated runs in which the same file is baseline-flaky, the count stamp's `flakyHits` holds that file at 2.
- [ ] At the threshold, a staged allowlist proposal names the file and its hit count, and `.claude-tweaks/verify-scope.json` is unchanged until the proposal is approved.

Flaky results from baseline verification now count toward the flaky-allowlist escalation threshold.

Surface: infra

## Current State

Claude Code 2.1.283+ ships a built-in `/prompt-audit` command. It reads CLAUDE.md files, skills, agents, and custom commands, and flags instructions written for older models, stale paths, and contradictory rules (source in the original request below).

What claude-tweaks already has in this space:

- `/claude-tweaks:harness-health` (`plugin/skills/harness-health/SKILL.md`) audits `.claude/skills/*.md`, `.claude/rules/*.md` and CLAUDE.md against the codebase, a template, and best practice, one target per firing. It then files `by:harness-health` issues. Its stated scope is the project's own `.claude/` tree (this repo has 17 files under `.claude/skills/`), not the 39 shipped `plugin/skills/*/SKILL.md` files. Its target discovery reads only `<root>/.claude/skills` (`plugin/bin/lib/harness-health/scope.js:198`).
- `docs/skill-authoring.md`'s "Model-version prompting notes" section (line 215) is a manual checklist to re-run whenever a new Claude model ships. It covers model-version deltas and a verification/self-check instruction audit against `docs/reference/claude-quality-levers.md`. That is the "instructions written for older models" concern, done by hand.

So the open question has two parts: what `/prompt-audit` catches that neither harness-health nor the manual model-version checklist catches, and whether it reaches the shipped `plugin/skills/` library at all.

## Deliverables

1. Run `/prompt-audit` once against this repo's CLAUDE.md, `.claude/skills/`, `plugin/skills/`, and `plugin/agents/`, and keep its raw output.
2. A comparison, posted as a comment on this record, that sorts each finding into one of three buckets:
   - already covered by harness-health (name the harness-health check);
   - already covered by the model-version prompting checklist in `docs/skill-authoring.md`;
   - genuinely new.
3. For each genuinely new finding, take exactly one of two routes:
   - a backlog record via `/claude-tweaks:capture` with a spec-shaped body, either fixing the flagged instruction or extending harness-health or the checklist to catch that class;
   - a stated reason, in the comment, why it is not worth acting on.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `/prompt-audit` has been run once over the targets in Deliverable 1. The comment states the Claude Code version used and the target set actually covered.
- Every finding in the run's output appears in the comparison comment under exactly one of the three buckets.
- Every genuinely new finding has either a linked filed backlog record or a stated reason for no action; none is left unrouted.
- The comment states whether `/prompt-audit` reached the `plugin/skills/` library, since harness-health does not.

## Release Note

No user-facing change. This produces an internal comparison of Claude Code's `/prompt-audit` against claude-tweaks' own harness-health audit.

## Technical Approach

Run `/prompt-audit` from an interactive session at the repo root. Then work through its findings against two references: harness-health's analysis criteria (`plugin/skills/_shared/harness-health-analysis.md`, the shared judge procedure) and the model-version checklist. Fixes to individual skills are not made in this record; they are filed as follow-ups so each lands with its own conformance-test run.

### Key Files

- `plugin/skills/harness-health/SKILL.md` — the existing audit whose coverage is compared
- `plugin/skills/_shared/harness-health-analysis.md` — harness-health's shared judge procedure
- `docs/skill-authoring.md` — the manual model-version prompting checklist (line 215)
- `docs/reference/claude-quality-levers.md` — the levers that checklist audits against

## Gotchas

- ASSUMPTION — verify at build: `/prompt-audit` can be run on demand in this environment and accepts the `plugin/` subtree as a target. It is a built-in slash command, so a headless agent may not be able to invoke it the same way. Confirm before relying on an unattended run.
- Fixing a flagged skill instruction here would touch shipped prose that conformance tests pin repo-wide (`tests/` byte-pins skill text). That is why fixes go to follow-up records, each with its own full-suite run.
- harness-health's own scope is `.claude/` by design. A finding that it misses on `plugin/skills/` is a scope question, not automatically a harness-health defect.

## Original request

Run /prompt-audit against claude-tweaks' own CLAUDE.md and skills

Current State:
- Claude Code's /prompt-audit (v2.1.283+) reads CLAUDE.md files, skills, agents, and custom commands, flagging instructions written for older models, stale paths, and contradictory rules.
- claude-tweaks ships a large skill library that has not been audited against the new Opus 5.5 / Sonnet 5.5 models this way.
- claude-tweaks' own harness-health skill does a related but not identical audit.

Deliverables:
- Run /prompt-audit prompt-audit against claude-tweaks' own repo.
- Compare its findings against what harness-health already catches; fold in anything harness-health misses.

Acceptance Criteria:
- /prompt-audit run once with findings reviewed.
- Any genuinely new findings (not already covered by harness-health) turned into follow-up fixes or a harness-health improvement.

Source: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/changelog#2-1-283

## Current State

#2741 added `plugin/bin/lib/skill-audit/harness-cost.js`. Its `measureAgentToolCost(repoRoot)` (lines 81-98) reads each `agents/{name}.md`'s `tools:` frontmatter and returns `[]` when no `agents/` directory exists. The function is exported (`:149`) and covered by `tests/bin-lib/skill-audit/harness-cost.test.js`, but nothing in production calls it. `grep -rln measureAgentToolCost plugin tests` returns only the module itself and its unit test.

`estimateHarnessCost(repoRoot)` (`:120-133`) builds its `entries` from `measureSkillToolCost` alone and returns `{ entries, totalSkills, unscopedCount }`. That function is the one consumed by `plugin/bin/harness-cost-report.js` (header comment `:18-19`: `entries` is "every skill's" record) and by `/claude-tweaks:harness-health`'s Harness cost-efficiency check (`plugin/skills/harness-health/SKILL.md:96-101`, which runs that CLI every firing).

The documentation advertises more than is reported. `docs/plugin-structure.md:23` says harness-cost.js measures each shipped skill's `allowed-tools:` count "(and each agent definition's `tools:`)". In practice `plugin/agents/qa-agent.md` (`tools: Bash`) never appears in any report. #2741's own deliverables named subagents ("so bloated skill or subagent definitions are visible"), so this is unmet scope, not a deliberate omission. The v6.134.0 release review found it (lens 3e, reproduced by both agents).

## Deliverables

1. Make `estimateHarnessCost` include agent definitions via `measureAgentToolCost`, with each entry distinguishable from skill entries (for example a `kind: 'skill' | 'agent'` field). Agent entries carry `tools`, `toolCount` and `overageRatio`. Size the agent file's bytes the same way skills are sized; shared-citation depth can be `null` or omitted for agents if it does not apply. Add an agent count to the summary alongside `totalSkills`.
2. Update `plugin/bin/harness-cost-report.js` so its output and `flagHighToolCount` handling cover agent entries. A high-tool-count agent can then be flagged the same way a skill is.
3. Update `/claude-tweaks:harness-health`'s cost-efficiency check prose (`SKILL.md:96-101`) to say agents are reported alongside skills.
4. Reconcile `docs/plugin-structure.md:23`, and the CLI line at `:128` if it describes output shape, with what is now reported.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `node plugin/bin/harness-cost-report.js --plugin-root plugin` output includes an entry for the `qa-agent` agent definition, marked as an agent rather than a skill.
- A test in `tests/bin-lib/skill-audit/harness-cost.test.js` fails if `estimateHarnessCost` stops including agent entries. Prove it goes red by removing the agent wiring.
- A fixture with no `agents/` directory still produces a valid report with zero agent entries and no error.
- `npm test` passes in full.

## Release Note

The harness cost report now includes subagent tool scopes alongside skills, as its documentation already claimed.

## Technical Approach

Concatenate `measureAgentToolCost(repoRoot)` results into `estimateHarnessCost`'s entries with a `kind` discriminator, then sort the combined list by bytes as today. Check every consumer of `entries` (the report CLI and any test fixtures pinning the JSON shape) before changing the shape. The change is additive, so existing skill-entry fields stay identical.

### Key Files

- `plugin/bin/lib/skill-audit/harness-cost.js` — `estimateHarnessCost`: include agent entries with a `kind` field and an agent summary count
- `plugin/bin/harness-cost-report.js` — report and flag agent entries; update the output-shape header comment
- `plugin/skills/harness-health/SKILL.md` — cost-efficiency check prose (96-101)
- `docs/plugin-structure.md` — reconcile lines 23 and 128 with the reported shape
- `tests/bin-lib/skill-audit/harness-cost.test.js` — agent-inclusion and no-agents-directory tests

## Gotchas

- `agents/` is a flat directory of `{name}.md` files, unlike `skills/{name}/SKILL.md`. Do not reuse `measuredBytes(path.join(dir, name, 'SKILL.md'))` for agents.
- `totalSkills` keeps meaning skills only. Add a separate agent count rather than changing its meaning, since harness-health's prose and any downstream reader treat it as a skill tally.
- `MINIMAL_BASELINE_TOOLS` was calibrated as a skill baseline. Note in the report or docs whether the same four-tool baseline is meaningful for agents (`qa-agent` declares `Bash` only) rather than implying an equivalence nobody validated.

## Original request

harness-cost: measureAgentToolCost is never wired into the report, though docs say agent tools: are measured

## Current State

`#2741` added `plugin/bin/lib/skill-audit/harness-cost.js`. `measureAgentToolCost` (line ~81) is implemented, exported and unit-tested, but has no production caller: `estimateHarnessCost` — the only function `bin/harness-cost-report.js` and harness-health's cost-efficiency check consume — maps over `measureSkillToolCost` alone. `docs/plugin-structure.md:23` says the module measures "each agent definition's `tools:`" and is called at runtime, so the agent half is advertised but never reported; `plugin/agents/qa-agent.md` (`tools: Bash`) is never measured. #2741's Deliverables name subagents ("so bloated skill or subagent definitions are visible"), so this is unmet scope, not a deliberate omission. Found by the v6.134.0 release review (lens 3e, reproduced by both agents, refutation not-refuted; ledger row 6).

## Deliverables

- [ ] `estimateHarnessCost` (or the report CLI) includes agent definitions' `tools:` cost via `measureAgentToolCost`, distinguishable from skill entries
- [ ] harness-health's cost-efficiency check reports agent entries alongside skills
- [ ] `docs/plugin-structure.md`'s description matches what is actually reported

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `node plugin/bin/harness-cost-report.js --plugin-root plugin` output includes an entry for `plugin/agents/qa-agent.md`
- [ ] A test fails if `estimateHarnessCost` stops including agent entries

Surface: infra

**Related:** #2679 (a practice to re-audit verification prompts on Claude model bumps — adjacent but distinct: that record is about verification-prompt wording specifically, this one is about skill/description trimming)

## Current State

External guidance (attributed to newer-model best-practice advice) argues that skill descriptions should shrink and that pre-reading doc stacks written for older, weaker models should stop, on the premise that a more capable model needs less hand-holding prose to trigger and use a skill correctly. claude-tweaks currently has ~40+ skills, many with substantial `SKILL.md` files and multi-file lazy-loaded sub-documents (per `docs/skill-authoring.md`'s conventions), whose descriptions and content depth have not been audited against this specific guidance.

## Deliverables

Audit a representative sample of claude-tweaks' skill descriptions and frontmatter against the trimming guidance, and produce findings: which descriptions carry verbosity that no longer earns its keep for a newer model, and which genuinely need their current depth (a skill whose triggering accuracy or correctness depends on detailed disambiguation, not verbosity for its own sake). Apply trims only where the finding is clear-cut; leave ambiguous cases as documented findings for a human decision rather than trimming speculatively.

## Acceptance Criteria

- At least a representative sample of skill descriptions/frontmatter (not necessarily all ~40+) is reviewed against the guidance, with findings stated per-skill (trim / keep-as-is / needs-human-judgment), not a blanket assertion.
- Any trims actually applied preserve triggering accuracy — verified by checking the trimmed description still matches this project's own skill-selection conventions (`docs/skill-authoring.md`'s Frontmatter conventions section) and doesn't remove disambiguating detail that exists for a documented reason (e.g. distinguishing near-identical skill names).
- Findings and any applied changes are summarized in the record's own closing report or a linked doc, not left implicit in a diff alone.

## Release Note

Trimmed skill descriptions that no longer help newer models pick the right skill.

## Technical Approach
